title: sre-watch-changeover-tactical-notes-2026-08-04
content:
Watch changeover notes (APAC night -> EU morning)
Date: 2026-08-04
Primary owner: Priya Nandakumar (offshore night to EU morning handover)
Secondary: Diego Ramos (on-call)
Shift length: 2300-0700 PDT (converted timestamps below are UTC+0 for clarity)

Executive summary:
- No Sev1/Sev2 during the watch window, but observed two medium-impact latency clusters tied to the prefix cache eviction edge case. Impacted customers: small fraction of hosted-api traffic on model gptx-13b-q.
- Immediate mitigations applied (temporary KV Cache threshold bump and rolling restart of edge-proxy group alpha-1).
- Short-term follow-ups assigned to infra and serving-runtime teams. Runbook gaps identified for cache-threshold tuning and for handling cache-heavy burst patterns.

Key metrics during shift (UTC):
- 00:00 - 07:00 UTC (primary observations window)
  - P95 latency (generation endpoints): 820ms -> peak 1.6s (two spikes at 01:18 and 04:42)
  - Error rate (5xx): baseline 0.12% -> peaked 0.9% for ~6 minutes at 04:42
  - Autoscaler churn: 3 scale events (cold-start deferrals visible in logs)
  - KV Cache evictions: small cluster where eviction rate jumped from 0.8% -> 6.1% per minute correlated to long-tail prefix churn

Timeline (UTC):
- 00:12 - Routine health checks ok. No action.
- 01:18 - Increase in P95 observed; downstream queueing on edge-proxy group alpha-1. Alerts: latency-warning (pager).
  - Action: Marcus restarted alpha-1 proxy pool (rolling restart). Temporary latency reduction observed but not to baseline.
- 01:32 - Investigation shows KV cache eviction spike on nodes serving gptx-13b-q; cache hitrate dropped 12pp. Suspected cause: concurrent burst of requests with high variety of prefixes from internal traffic test job (job id: loadtest/2026-08-03-22).
  - Action: Disabled non-critical internal job (loadtest) and increased KV cache max_entries on affected nodes by +25% as a hotfix.
- 04:05 - Small uptick in 5xxs; traced to one model shard crossing memory threshold and triggering swapback; logs show 'kv_evict_overtime' warnings. Node rebooted (node-hr-07) to reclaim kernel memory; service returned to normal.
- 04:42 - Secondary spike: short (~6m) burst of 5xxs and latency. Root cause appears to be a mis-scheduled maintenance job that ran across multiple regions (ticket: JIRA-OPS-7281).
  - Action: Kicked off emergency rollback of that maintenance job and applied conservative rate-limiting at the routing layer for gptx-13b-q for 20 minutes.
- 06:30 - All metrics trending back to baseline. Post-shift checks run and noted outstanding follow-ups.

Observed patterns and plausible root causes:
- Pattern #1: Prefix cache churn due to non-production traffic (internal loadtests) colliding with production traffic for memory-limited shards. This leads to increased eviction, increased KV cache misses, and higher token generation latency.
- Pattern #2: Incomplete coordination between maintenance scheduler and region-aware routing -> simultaneous maintenance across multiple AZs triggered cascading resource pressure.

Immediate mitigations applied (summary):
- Rolling restart of edge-proxy pool alpha-1 (Marcus) -> partial relief.
- Disabled internal loadtest (Priya) -> reduced bursty prefix diversity.
- Increased KV cache max_entries on affected nodes (temporary +25%) -> improved hit rate for the rest of the watch.
- Emergency rate-limit rule applied for gptx-13b-q on global router (Diego) for 20m -> prevented further SLO breaches.

Runbook gaps identified (actionable):
1) KV Cache Tuning runbook lacks guidance on emergency threshold bump (how much to bump per node class and when to revert). Need explicit rollback steps to avoid long-term memory bloat.
2) Maintenance scheduler runbook needs a pre-check to ensure maintenance windows are region-staggered for multi-AZ services.
3) Edge-proxy restart play: we have no quick healthcheck that verifies KV cache behavior post-restart; add post-restart cache validation step.

Open action items (owners and due dates):
- OPS-1: Draft KV Cache emergency bump + rollback procedure and add to runbook (owner: Anita Chen, due: 2026-08-07).
- OPS-2: Add a pre-flight check into maintenance scheduler to verify regional stagger (owner: Marcus O'Leary, due: 2026-08-09).
- OPS-3: Add a post-restart KV cache validation script to edge-proxy tooling (owner: Diego Ramos, due: 2026-08-10).
- OPS-4: Identify and quarantine internal traffic sources that mimic production prefixes (owner: Priya Nandakumar, due: 2026-08-06).
- OPS-5: Follow up with platform-insights team to instrument more granular shard-level memory metrics (owner: Diego Ramos, due: 2026-08-12).

Follow-ups completed during watch:
- Disabled offending internal job; verified drop in eviction rate (Priya).
- Performed controlled restart of alpha-1 proxy group and monitoring (Marcus).

Notes for incoming shift (EU morning):
- Watch context: keep an eye on gptx-13b-q routing rule (we temporarily tightened rate-limits). If P95 stays >1s for >10 minutes, escalate to serving-runtime oncall (pager escalation path in runbook).
- Node-hr-07 remains under observation after reboot (oom_kill traces cleared but devops will run deeper memory diagnostics tomorrow).
- Do not re-enable internal loadtest until OPS-4 completed and confirmed safe (we left a placeholder in the scheduler to block it). Calendar: loadtest flagged in "internal-jobs/blocklist" until cleared.
- Run the lightweight post-restart cache validation script (added to tools/runbooks) once per proxy pool restart. Script path: github.com/redwood-inference/tools/blob/main/cache-healthcheck.sh

Communication log (who we messaged and where):
- Slack: #sre-watch (continuous updates)
- Pager duty: triggered for latency-warning and follow-up for on-call (acknowledged)
- Notified product-ops and customer-success of brief blips affecting a subset of hosted-api customers via #prod-notify at 04:55 UTC.

Attachments & traces to review:
- Traces: trace-id 8b1f3a2a-2026-08-04-01-18 (KV miss heavy)
- Logs: s3://redwood-logs/2026/08/04/edge-alpha1-evict.log
- Related PR (serving-runtime): github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/451 - minor fix for kv eviction metrics emission

Suggested post-mortem candidates (if follow-ups not completed within 72h):
- Post-mortem candidate A: Cross-region maintenance scheduler incident (if OPS-2 not done by 2026-08-11).
- Post-mortem candidate B: Persistent KV cache degradation leading to customer SLO breaches (if OPS-1/OPS-3 not completed by 2026-08-10).

Misc notes and quick wins:
- Consider adding a "non-prod prefix isolation" flag in the router so internal tests never hit production cache keyspace in the future. Low-effort, high-impact.
- Short-term: set a temporary global soft-cap on cache evictions per-minute and alert on sustained >2% minute-over-minute evictions.

Handoff checklist (for incoming oncall):
- [ ] Confirm rate-limit for gptx-13b-q is set to the temporary threshold (check router rules).
- [ ] Validate node-hr-07 health and ensure diagnostics are scheduled.
- [ ] Verify internal loadtests remain disabled and that the scheduler block is present.
- [ ] Scan alerts for any new bursts on prefix eviction metrics.
- [ ] Run the cache-healthcheck.sh if you perform any proxy restarts.

Contact info for follow-ups:
- Anita Chen (infra lead) - anita@redwood.ai
- Marcus O'Leary (oncall SRE) - marcus@redwood.ai
- Diego Ramos (runtime engineer) - diego@redwood.ai

Closing note: overall watch stabilized with temporary mitigations. Primary technical debt is runbook gaps around cache emergency handling and maintenance scheduling. Please drive OPS-1 through OPS-4 before next major rollout of gptx-13b-q.

-- Priya (handoff)
